primitives.name: Pairwise Logistic Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: The author shows ESPN's conventional park factor (home/road ratio) is confounded and even degrades prediction for singles and walks, then proposes modeling every plate appearance as a matchup between a batting team and a pitching team plus a park, distilling the park effect via logistic regression.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_{i,j,k}': 'Probability of event given batting team i, pitching team j, and park k (dimensionless)', 'b_i': 'Batting strength of team i (log odds)', 'd_j': 'Pitching/defense strength of team j (log odds)', 'r_k': 'Park effect for venue k (log odds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Team strength is constant within a season; one scalar park effect per event; events modeled independently; home/away team–park index coincidence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular when any team has zero variance in performance, leading to perfect collinearity.

layer2.mapping: Maps to NFL venue effects: offensive team i becomes receiving team, defensive team j becomes defensive team, stadium k captures altitude/dome/wind effects. Event probabilities become P(TD, FG, explosive play, punt).
layer2.telemetry: Log-loss improvement over constant baseline for each football event.

primitives.name: Steepest Descent Fitting
primitives.verbatim_quote: Parameters fit by steepest descent on squared error J = Σ(p_{i,j,k} - x_l)2 (Eqs.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'J': 'Squared error loss function (dimensionless)', 'p_{i,j,k)': 'Predicted probability', 'x_l': 'Observed binary outcome (0 or 1)'}
primitives.assumptions: Gradient descent assumes convex loss surface; may converge slowly near optima.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails to guarantee maximum likelihood estimates; can produce biased park factors.

layer2.mapping: In NFL context, replace with Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) to obtain unbiased stadium parameters. Penalized MLE with L2 regularization stabilizes estimates for low-count venues.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence rate and final log-loss compared to MLE baseline.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core issue is separating venue effects from team-specific performance. Standard park factors conflate these, leading to biased estimates. By modeling each PA as a trilinear form, we isolate the park term. However, steepest descent is a proxy for MLE and can degrade accuracy. NFL venue analysis requires adapting the event set (touchdowns, field goals) and using proper MLE with identifiability constraints to avoid overfitting.
